as_read: Thirteen labels print kudzu root extract and one prints Pueraria mirifica root extract; the stored trial tested isolated puerarin, and small kudzu extract trials on alcohol intake conflict.

quote.text: In contrast to results from prior studies among non-treatment-seeking young adult men, kudzu did not perform better than placebo in reducing drinking among a treatment-seeking sample of men and women with AUD.

proposed_decision_text: These labels print kudzu root extract, most at 1200 mg, or kudzu with kudzu extract, and one complex prints Pueraria mirifica root extract at 80 mg; none prints isolated puerarin, and the 13 kudzu labels carry no positioning category. This review read abstracts only. The stored crossover pilot gave isolated puerarin 1200 mg daily to 10 volunteers and saw fewer beers in one drinking session, names no primary outcome, and tested a single isoflavone rather than the extract (PMID 22578529). A kudzu extract crossover trial in heavy drinkers reports fewer beers after 7 days, but its abstract states no dose, sample size or primary outcome (PMID 15897719). An eight-week double-blind placebo-controlled study of kudzu extract with 750 mg isoflavones in 19 treatment-seeking adults found no advantage over placebo, names no primary outcome, and does not state randomization in the abstract (PMID 42779941). A kudzu root extract study in 50 postmenopausal women was open-label with no placebo and reports change from baseline, with capsule doses not stated in the abstract (PMID 34744740). A puerarin tablet study at 150 mg/d was added to Diane-35 and metformin, measured biomarkers and names no primary outcome (PMID 34032731). A hot flash trial tested kudzu flower with mandarin peel, a different plant part in a combination (PMID 33105861). A systematic review of Pueraria mirifica called its efficacy on menopausal symptoms inconclusive, citing methodological shortcomings and no standardization (PMID 29409850). No study read is a human randomized trial of the labeled kudzu root extract alone with a verified dose, a stated population and a named primary outcome with a direction.
clinician_items: 29409850: Pueraria mirifica review reports serum C-reactive protein doubled, with adverse events (mastodynia, vaginal spotting, dizziness) at similar rates across groups; one label (216948) prints P. mirifica and is positioned for women. Estrogenic botanical, worth a look at the pregnancy and hormone-sensitive lanes.
stored_rating_note: Stored positive_moderate and applicable_reviewed_trials rest on one 10-person crossover pilot of isolated puerarin; the labels print kudzu root extract, not puerarin, and the abstract names no primary outcome. The stored material_form does not match what these labels print. 42779941 (2026, null versus placebo) is not in the stored record.
unread_notes: Abstracts only. Two PubMed searches plus one exact-title lookup that returned 0 hits (the lookup was over the two-search limit); 15897719 was opened by a PMID recalled from memory, not from a search hit, and its title confirmed it. Two other recalled PMIDs (26048081, 10636418) were unrelated papers and are not cited. Later kudzu alcohol trials from the same group, including the four-week trial 42779941 refers to and a binge-drinking trial, were not located or read; Shebek 2000 pilot not read. Hits seen and not read: 38879879 (combination tablets), 37782173 (Gelanxinning capsule), 40413050 and 31651889 and 30616613 (protocols).
